Summary: Report Authoring
Description: Rangers create, save, validate, and submit reports, including offline authoring. Traces to FR-01-FR-03 and FR-06-FR-12.

Summary: Review & Approval
Description: Supervisors and the law enforcement liaison review reports in the required sequence. Traces to FR-04, FR-13-FR-17, FR-30-FR-31, and FR-33.

Summary: Dissemination
Description: Approved reports are delivered to selected partners with recipient-specific disclosure controls. Traces to FR-05, FR-18-FR-24, FR-29, and FR-32.

Summary: Administration
Description: Administrators maintain user access, sensitive species, and report templates. Traces to FR-25-FR-27.

Summary: Audit & Records
Description: Report actions and disclosures are recorded for accountability. Traces to FR-28.

Summary: Ranger saves a report as a draft
Description: As a field ranger, I want to save a partially completed report as a draft, so that I can finish it later without losing my work. Traces to FR-02 / TR-02.1-02.6.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am logged in as a ranger and at least one report field has a value | WHEN I save the report as a draft | THEN it is saved with Draft status, appears in My Drafts, and displays a confirmation. || GIVEN a saved draft | WHEN I reopen it | THEN all previously saved field values and photos are restored. || GIVEN I am logged in as a ranger and no report field has a value | WHEN I attempt to save the report as a draft | THEN no draft is created and nothing is added to My Drafts.

Summary: Supervisor sends each partner an authorized report version
Description: As a supervisor, I want to select report recipients and send each only the version authorized for their recipient category and report context, so that partners get the information they need without seeing data they are not cleared for. Traces to FR-05 / TR-05.1-05.7 and FR-29.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN an approved report with recipient-specific disclosure rules | WHEN a supervisor selects recipients and sends it | THEN each recipient receives only their authorized version. || GIVEN a recipient is not authorized to see a field | WHEN the recipient opens the report or its API response | THEN the value is withheld or generalized server-side and no unauthorized original value is present. || GIVEN a recipient receives a disseminated copy | WHEN the system records the send | THEN the recipient, timestamp, and disclosure outcome for each data class are logged.

Summary: Ranger creates a report from a standard template
Description: As a field ranger, I want to start from a standard report template and select multiple incident types, so that one report can accurately describe a combined incident. Traces to FR-01 and FR-06.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am logged in as a ranger | WHEN I create a report | THEN a standard template is displayed. || GIVEN a new or draft report | WHEN I select two or more incident types | THEN the fields for every selected type are displayed on that report, including the structured evidence fields when poaching is selected.

Summary: Ranger authors reports offline
Description: As a field ranger, I want to create, edit, and save reports without a network connection, so that field conditions do not prevent reporting. Traces to FR-07.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN my device has no network connection | WHEN I create, edit, and save a report | THEN my changes are saved locally and remain available after closing and reopening the app.

Summary: Offline-submitted reports sync when connected
Description: As a field ranger, I want reports submitted offline to transmit when connectivity returns, so that reports reach the agency system without re-entry. Traces to FR-08.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report was submitted while the device was offline | WHEN network connectivity becomes available | THEN the report is transmitted to the server and its sync state is shown to the ranger.

Summary: Ranger attaches report photos
Description: As a field ranger, I want to attach photos to a report, so that reviewers and authorized partners can inspect supporting evidence. Traces to FR-09.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am editing a report | WHEN I attach a supported photo | THEN it is associated with that report and remains available when the report is reopened.

Summary: System assigns each report a unique report number
Description: As a ranger or supervisor, I want each report to have a unique identifier, so that it can be referenced consistently. Traces to FR-10 / TR-10.1-10.4.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I create a report | WHEN it is created offline | THEN it receives a unique internal identifier and displays Number pending. || GIVEN the report syncs | WHEN the server accepts it | THEN it assigns a unique number in NR-YYYY-NNNNN format.

Summary: Ranger submits only complete and attested reports
Description: As a supervisor, I want reports checked for required fields and ranger attestation, including evidence fields for every selected incident type, so that incomplete reports do not enter review. Traces to FR-03 / TR-03.1-03.4, FR-11, and FR-12.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report has multiple incident types including poaching | WHEN any required core, selected-type, or structured evidence field is missing or the ranger has not attested | THEN submission is blocked and the missing fields are identified. || GIVEN all applicable required fields and attestation are complete | WHEN the ranger submits | THEN the report is accepted for review. || GIVEN an incomplete report is submitted through the API | WHEN the server validates it | THEN it returns HTTP 422 with missing fields and does not accept the report.

Summary: Administrator manages user accounts and roles
Description: As a system administrator, I want to manage user accounts and role assignments, so that system access matches agency responsibilities. Traces to FR-25.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am an authorized administrator | WHEN I add or update a user and assign a role | THEN the account and role assignment are saved and reflected in that user's access.

Summary: Administrator maintains sensitive species list
Description: As a system administrator, I want to maintain the sensitive species list, so that disclosure rules use current species protections. Traces to FR-26.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am an authorized administrator | WHEN I add, update, or remove a species from the sensitive list | THEN the current list is saved and used for subsequent disclosure decisions.

Summary: System records report actions in an audit log
Description: As a records officer, I want views, changes, approvals, and sends recorded with the actor and time, so that report handling is auditable. Traces to FR-28 and NFR-12.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a user views, changes, approves, or sends a report | WHEN the action occurs | THEN an audit entry records the actor, action, report, and timestamp. || GIVEN an audit entry exists | WHEN any user, including an administrator, attempts to edit or delete it | THEN the entry remains unchanged.

Summary: Supervisor approves or rejects a submitted report
Description: As a supervisor, I want to approve a submitted report or return it with a categorized comment, so that the report has a documented review outcome. Traces to FR-04 / TR-04.1-04.5.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am the assigned supervisor or active delegate and the report is Submitted | WHEN I approve it | THEN its status changes to Approved, or to Pending Liaison Review if the report includes poaching, and the action is recorded. || GIVEN the same conditions | WHEN I reject without a comment or reason category | THEN the rejection is refused. || GIVEN I reject with a comment and reason category | WHEN the action is saved | THEN status changes to Returned and the comment, category, reviewer, and timestamp are stored.

Summary: Assigned reviewers receive notifications and an action queue
Description: As an assigned reviewer, I want notification of reports awaiting action and a queue that identifies overdue items, so that I can act promptly. Traces to FR-17 and FR-30. Note: the overdue threshold is pending Dana (spec open question #6).
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report enters my review queue | WHEN it awaits my action | THEN I receive a notification. || GIVEN I open my review list | WHEN reports are awaiting action | THEN the list shows them and identifies reports that meet the configured overdue rule.

Summary: Supervisor delegates review authority
Description: As a supervisor, I want to delegate review authority to a designated backup for a defined period, so that reports continue to be reviewed during my absence. Traces to FR-31 and TR-04.1.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am an authorized supervisor | WHEN I designate a backup and define a start and end time | THEN that delegate may approve or reject reports during the active period and not outside it. || GIVEN I am an active delegate | WHEN a report I authored is awaiting review | THEN I cannot approve or reject it.

Summary: Poaching reports receive liaison review before dissemination
Description: As a law enforcement liaison, I want supervisor-approved reports containing poaching to be routed to me for secondary review, so that evidence is checked before sharing. Traces to FR-13.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a supervisor approves a report that includes poaching, including a multi-type report | WHEN the approval is recorded | THEN the report enters Pending Liaison Review and cannot be disseminated until the liaison completes review.

Summary: Liaison approves or returns a poaching report
Description: As a law enforcement liaison, I want to approve or return a report under secondary review with a documented reason, so that only reports with usable evidence go to law enforcement. Traces to FR-33. Where a returned report goes (ranger or supervisor) is pending Dana (spec open question #14); this story assumes it returns to the ranger.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am the law enforcement liaison and a report is Pending Liaison Review | WHEN I approve it | THEN its status changes to Approved and it becomes available for dissemination. || GIVEN the same conditions | WHEN I return it without a comment or reason category | THEN the return is refused. || GIVEN I return it with a comment and reason category | WHEN the action is saved | THEN its status changes to Returned, the comment, category, reviewer, and timestamp are stored, and the authoring ranger is notified.

Summary: Ranger receives rejection notice
Description: As a field ranger, I want to be notified when my report is rejected, so that I can correct and resubmit it. Traces to FR-14.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN my report is rejected | WHEN the rejection is saved | THEN I am notified with the rejection comment.

Summary: Ranger receives notice when a submitted report changes
Description: As a field ranger, I want to be notified when another user modifies my submitted report, so that I know its contents have changed. Traces to FR-16.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN another user modifies my submitted report | WHEN the change is saved | THEN I am notified of the modification.

Summary: Submitted reports retain revision history
Description: As a supervisor or records officer, I want every change to a submitted report recorded with its author and time, so that the report's history can be reconstructed. Traces to FR-15.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a submitted report is changed | WHEN the change is saved | THEN the system retains the prior revision and records the changed content, actor, and timestamp.

Summary: Ranger sends a minimal urgent notice to a rehabilitation veterinarian
Description: As a field ranger, I want to send a minimal urgent animal-care notice before report approval, so that a veterinarian can arrange care without receiving unrelated sensitive data. Traces to FR-18 / TR-18.1-18.5.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report includes injured wildlife | WHEN I send an urgent notice, including while the report is a draft | THEN the notice contains only species, number of animals, condition, permitted pickup location, and ranger contact. || GIVEN the device is offline | WHEN I queue the notice | THEN the app clearly shows Queued, prioritizes it at next sync, and records its eventual send.

Summary: Partner opens a report using email-code verification
Description: As a partner recipient, I want to access an approved report without creating an account or password, so that I can securely retrieve information shared with me. Traces to FR-19, NFR-09, and NFR-11.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report has been shared with my email address | WHEN I open its access link | THEN I must verify using a one-time code sent to that address before viewing my authorized report version. || GIVEN I open the access link | WHEN I enter an incorrect one-time code | THEN the report is not displayed. || GIVEN the access link has passed its expiry period | WHEN I open it | THEN the report is not displayed and I am told the link has expired.

Summary: Supervisor approves a one-time disclosure exception
Description: As a supervisor, I want to approve an exception for a specific recipient with a recorded reason, so that exceptional disclosure is controlled and accountable. Traces to FR-20.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a recipient requires a disclosure exception | WHEN an authorized supervisor approves it with a reason | THEN only that recipient's report version applies the approved exception and the decision is auditable.

Summary: Partner acknowledges report receipt
Description: As a designated partner recipient, I want to acknowledge receipt of a shared report, so that the agency can confirm delivery. Traces to FR-21.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I have opened a shared report | WHEN I acknowledge receipt | THEN the system records the recipient and acknowledgement timestamp.

Summary: Partner downloads a recipient-marked PDF
Description: As a partner recipient, I want to download my authorized report version as a PDF, so that I can retain it for authorized case work. Traces to FR-22 and FR-32.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I have access to a shared report | WHEN I download it as a PDF | THEN it contains only my authorized version and is marked with my recipient name and the download date and time.

Summary: System flags federally protected species notification deadline
Description: As a records officer, I want reports involving federally protected species flagged with the applicable notification deadline, so that required notifications are not missed. Traces to FR-23; deadline value pending verification by Marcus Webb.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN a report involves a federally protected species and the verified deadline rule is configured | WHEN the report is saved | THEN the applicable notification deadline is displayed. || GIVEN the deadline rule is not verified | WHEN the feature is configured | THEN no unconfirmed deadline is presented as authoritative.

Summary: Administrator configures default recipient categories
Description: As a system administrator, I want to define default recipient categories by incident type, so that supervisors can prepare consistent distributions while retaining final control. Traces to FR-24.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN an administrator configures recipient defaults for an incident type | WHEN a supervisor prepares an approved report of that type | THEN the suggested recipient list is prefilled and requires supervisor confirmation before sending.

Summary: Administrator updates report templates without a software release
Description: As a system administrator, I want to add or modify template fields and mark them required, so that reporting needs can be maintained without a software release. Traces to FR-27.
Acceptance Criteria: GIVEN I am an authorized administrator | WHEN I add or modify a template field or its required status | THEN the updated template is available to new reports without deploying new application code.
